newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm, eye US data.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm, eye US data.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds firmed in lively trading, mainly on foreign buying and position-squaring, but dealers said on Monday the market was largely on the sidelines ahead of U.S. statistics due this week.
"Buying interest is seen from London, Russia is mainly selling. It looks like everybody is trying to keep flat positions ahead of the data," National Reserve Bank dealer Andrei Ivanov-Golitsyn.

Important U.S. data will be released this week, which will be closely watched for signs of inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy. On Tuesday the first quarter Employment Cost Index and April consumer confidence figures surface.
On Wednesday, gross domestic product (GDP) for the first quarter is released. The April NAPM report comes on Thursday, and on Friday the all-important employment report for April will hit the market.
On May 20 the U.S. policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets and could raise U.S. interest rates.
"MinFins are firmer as some people could think that the market is oversold but there are no fundamental reasons to buy," a Moscow Narodny Bank dealer said.
But Ivanov-Golitsyn said some optimism in lively trading could surge on expectations Russia will receive money from the IMF in May or soon after.

IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said on Thursday the IMF board was likely to approve the 1997 part of Russia's three-year programme in May and payments of the loan would resume soon afterwards.
